question: Will a hurricane be active in the Eastern Pacific at any point between October 15 and October 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Rachel (70 kt Oct 7) forecast post-tropical by ~Oct 11, so it cannot count. YES hinges on EP92/future Simon (90% genesis, TD within ~1 day, slow WNW off southern Mexico, models eventually take it into Mexico; media only forecast TS strength) still being a hurricane 7-9 days after genesis, or a 30%-in-7-day disturbance south of Guatemala forming early next week and reaching hurricane strength by Oct 17. Climatological base rate of an EPac hurricane active Oct 15-17 is ~15% (higher ~25-30% in El Nino years like 2009, 2015). Combining paths gives ~22%. No matching human market found (Polymarket Cat5-record market is unrelated).

calls.reasoning: Base rate: from my recollection of past seasons (not a counted dataset), roughly 20-25% of years had an EPac hurricane active Oct 15-17, a bit higher in El Nino years. Rachel (70 kt, 20.4N 120.3W) is forecast to weaken to a TS by Oct 7 evening and go post-tropical by Oct 10, so it cannot count. Invest 92E (90% formation, at 13.1N 99.2W, moving slowly WNW-NW near the SW Mexico coast) would become Simon; forecasts of its moisture reaching New Mexico early next week suggest recurvature or landfall around Oct 11-13, so it would likely be dead before the window, though a slower or offshore track could keep it alive. A low south of Guatemala, expected early next week with only 30% 7-day odds, would need fast strengthening to be a hurricane by Oct 17. No matching human market was found; the Polymarket Category 5 record market is a different contract.

calls.reasoning: Rachel (70 kt, 20.4N 120.4W at 07/03Z) is forecast below hurricane strength by Oct 8 and post-tropical by Oct 11, so it cannot satisfy the Oct 15-17 window. The main path is future Simon (EP92, 90% formation in 48h), which may reach hurricane strength, but model tracks bring it north along or into western Mexico, so it would need to persist offshore at hurricane strength about a week after forming. A second disturbance south of Guatemala (30% in 7 days, forming early next week) would need fast intensification to be a hurricane by Oct 17. Climatological base rate for a hurricane in a given mid-October 3-day window is roughly 25-35%, higher in El Nino; specific timing of current candidates is mildly unfavorable. calls.reasoning: Rachel (Cat 1, 20.4N 120.4W) is forecast post-tropical by ~Oct 11 and cannot count. Future Simon (92E, about to become a TD off SW Mexico, slow WNW-NW) is forecast by models to track into Mexico, with moisture reaching NM ~Oct 12-13, so it is likely dissipated before Oct 15; persistence offshore at hurricane strength ~8%. A second disturbance south of Guatemala (30%/7d, forming ~Oct 12-13) would need genesis plus rapid intensification by Oct 17: ~10%. Genesis beyond the 7-day horizon adds ~3%. The total, ~20%, is slightly below a ~25-30% El Nino mid-October climatology because the timing of the known candidates is unfavorable.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on all facts: Rachel cannot count, 92E has 90% genesis odds and its models track into Mexico, and the second area is at 30%/7d. They disagreed on the base rate (15% vs 20-25% vs 25-35%), none of which came from counted data, and on how to weigh Simon's track. I checked the NHC EPac page: only Rachel is active (80 mph, adv #40) and no Simon advisory or intensity forecast exists yet. Zoom Earth: 92E at 30 mph and 1006 mb, moving slowly WNW-NW, no landfall timing. A Fox Weather search confirmed models take future-Simon into Mexico. I tried to fetch the New Mexico blog for timing, but the request was blocked by a Google captcha, so the Oct 12-13 moisture timing is unverified. With no new factual tiebreak, I built the estimate from paths (Simon ~8%, second area ~10%, other ~3%), which gives ~19%. The Polymarket Cat-5 record market is unrelated; no matching human market exists.
